1  JUDGMENT
The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 06-10-2021 at about 9.00 to 9.15 a.m. the petitioner was riding his two wheeler bearing registration No.KA-05-HL-6386 on Maruthi Circle towards Ganesh Bhavan, when he reached near Sathish Stores, at that time driver of Car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-3124 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle. Due to the forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to ESI hospital for first aid, then shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery.
4. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-M-3124.
Hence, Basavanagudi Traffic Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.73/2021 under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
5. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 & 2 appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.
6. In the written statement of the respondent No.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further stated that he is the RC owner of the offending vehicle,
the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and it is valid as on the date of accident.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further, contended that, this respondent admits about issuance of Insurance policy in respect of Car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-3124 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that offending vehicle was not at all involved in this accident and falsely implicated the same in the alleged accident.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

Further contended that, as on the date of the accident the petitioner not wearing helmet with ISI Mark and he does not posses valid D.L. hence this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner.
Ultimately stated that the claim of the petitioner is Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.

2
highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 06-10-2021 at about 9-00 to 9-15 a.m. near Satish Stores,
Hanumanthanagara, Bengaluru 560 019, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-3124 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P21.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Medical Record Officer as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P22 to Ex.P24.
In addition to their evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Rahul P. as PW3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P25 & Ex.P26.
Further examined employer of the petitioner as PW4 and got marked the document at Ex.P27.
10. On the other hand, the respondents have not led any evidence on their behalf.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
13. It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-41-M- 3124, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently
he had sustained grievous injuries.
14. On the other hand, though the respondent No.2 being the insurance company filed written statement not seriously disputed the accident and its consequence.

But strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and also highlighted on the point of delay in giving first information about the accident and also disputed Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.

P on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52479710/
3 about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
15. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P12
. Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R. Ex.P2- true copy of first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex. P4
-true copy of spot sketch,
Ex.P5-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P6- true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P7-true copy of notice under section 133 of IMV Act, Ex.P8-true copy of the reply to notice under section 133 of IMV Act,

Ex.P9-copy of the notice issued to the accused, Ex.P10- copy of the reply given by the accused to Ex.P9, Ex.P11-true copy of charge sheet filed against the driver of the car under section 279 & 337 of IPC.
16.

On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Basavanagudi Traffic Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of IPC.

Based upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
17.
Per contra, respondent has contended that there is delay in lodging the complaint.
On going through the recitals of the complaint, it is forthcoming that, the complainant is none other the injured/petitioner.
In the complaint, he narrated clearly stated about the negligent act of the driver of the offending car which caused accident and injuries to him.

In the recitals of the Ex.P1 he clearly narrated that, after three days of the accident, he gave belated complaint as the complainant was taking treatment and also after verification of the vehicle number in CCTV Camera came to know that the vehicle number is KA-41-M-3124, hence, belated complaint has been lodged.

18. On going through the recitals of the complaint and the reasons given by the complainant about the delay in giving first information is concerned one can say that, if a person severely injured in the accident, one cannot expect immediate complaint about the accident instead of providing treatment.
Delay in giving first information always cannot be looked in a suspicious manner, the said point of delay is to be considered by looking into the each facts and circumstances and also the reasons set out in the complaint, on the point of delay.
Hence, I am of the view that the delay in giving first information about the accident in the case on hand is not fatal.

Moreover, on the point of delay it is necessary to note down the decision reported in (2011) 4 SCC Page 693, between, Ravi V/S.
Badrinarayan, "It was observed that, "delay in lodging F.I.R cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing that the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the police station immediately, after the accident.
As the family members give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the police station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the F.I.R with the police."

19. Apart from this, it is pertinent to discuss that, either the driver of the offending vehicle or the owner of the offending vehicle have not made an effort to challenge the recitals of the Ex.P2, well in time before the competent court of law.
Further, there is no contra materials available on record to Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.

P on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52479710/
4 impeach the recitals of Ex.P1.
20.

Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

21. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41- M-3124.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
22.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

23. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injury:-
Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.P on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52479710/
5 1) Two abrasion over right elbow measuring each 3x5 cms and 1x 3 cms 2) X-ray shows Right shoulder, right elbow and pelvis and bilateral hip , No evidence of fracure.
25.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are simple in nature.

Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary, OPD slip, doctors report,
outpatient record, x-rays as per Ex.P13 to Ex.P16 & Ex.P20.
On perusal of Ex.P13 discharge summary issued by M.S.Ramaiah Medical College Hospital, goes to show that petitioner was admitted on 17.2.2022 and discharged on 22.2.2022.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Medical Record Technician as PW2.
PW2 has placed police intimation and MLC extract along with authorisation letter at Ex.P22 to Ex.P24.
In addition to their evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Rahul P., as PW3.
He has placed the case sheet and x-ray at Ex.P25 & Ex.P26.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
26.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a Laundry labour and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has placed the evidence of PW4.
PW4 has stated in his evidence that petitionr was working in his laundry shop as a daily wage clothes presser since 2010.
He left the job in the month of October 2021 due to accident.
He was earning Rs.500-Rs.600/- per day depending upon the workload.
Except his statement he has not placed any document to show that petitioner was working with his laundry shop and was earning Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day.
In the absence of the documents, it is apt to be considered notional income of the petitioner.
On going through the discharge summary marked at Ex.P13, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 17.2.2022 and discharged on 22.2.2022.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of one month by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
27.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P18 to the extent of Rs.10,654/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P19.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,654/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
28.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.

P on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52479710/
6
petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/-
towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
29.The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injury for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed wound certificate for consideration.

Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Rahul P.
examined as PW3.
PW3 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained right rotator cuff tear.
For which the petitioner underwent surgery for right rotator cuff repair on 19.2.2022.

Further,
PW2 has stated that, at the time of his examination of the petitioner on 11.4.2023 for assessment of disability, the petitioner has suffered 39% disability of right upper limb.
30. At the time of cross-examination of PW3, stated that he is the treated doctor and also denied the suggestion that he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
31. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW3 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW3 as 39% disability for the right upper limb.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3, it is apt to take whole body disability as 8%
instead of 39%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
32. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 40 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P17 for consideration.
On going through the said documents, the year of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 1981.
The accident occurred on 6.10.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 40 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '15' is to be taken into consideration.

33. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was was working as a laundry labour and getting an income of Rs.15,000/-.
In this regard, he has placed the evidence of PW4.
PW4 has stated that he is the employer of the M/s Srinivasa Dry Cleaners.
Further stated that petitioner was working in his laundry shop as a daily wage clothes presser since 2010.
He left the job in the month of october 2021 duye to the accident.
He was earning daily payment of Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day.
He has furnished the copy of the trade licence marked at Ex.P27.
Except his oral evidence he has not produced any document for exact income of the petitioner per month.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.

As per the notional Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.P on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52479710/
7 income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.

34. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,000 X 12 X 15 X 8/100= Rs.2,16,000/-.
Loss of amenities;
35.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he is facing serious restriction in movement of right hand shoulder and to do normal work and bearing weight for lifetime.
On perusal of evidence of PW3 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
36.
PW3 has not stated about the future medication and also not placed any documents for consideration.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

37. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads
Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 25,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 15,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs. 10,654-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 10,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.2,16,000-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 5,000-00 7.Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs.2,81,654-00 Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.

8 38.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,81,654/- (Rupees two lakh eighty one thousand six hundred and fifty four only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
LIABILITY:
39.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-41-M-3124 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
40. The respondent No.2 insurance company has admitted about the issuance of the policy and its validity.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
41.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,81,654/- (Rupees two lakh eighty one thousand six hundred and fifty four only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Hence, I am of the view that the delay in giving first information about the accident in the case on hand is not fatal.
Further, there is no contra materials available on record to Ashok vs Ramesh Kumar.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3, it is apt to take whole body disability as 8%
instead of 39%.

In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
